newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower as frost fears wane.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower as frost fears wane.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on diminished fears about frost damage soon to the U.S. soybean crop, traders said.

"If they were still talking freeze we would have been higher today. The only thing you can say for the bulls is we didn't take out $8.00 (November) today," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Some weather reports early Thursday had indicated potential frost in portions of the northern Midwest, including northern Iowa, by September 23 or September 24 -- which rallied the market Thursday.
But Friday, meteorologists said weather maps had shifted to a warmer scenario for the Midwest.
"Today's version (of the maps) does not infer a freeze on the (September) 23 or 24," said Fred Gesser chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.

Soybeans also were pressured by news this week that Brazil was eliminating a tax on exports. Some people thought the elimination of the export tax would go into effect on October 1 or November 1. But "it looks like it's effective immediately," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Soybeans closed three to 12-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with Sep down 7-1/4 at $8.28-1/2 and Nov down 12-1/2 at $8.02.

Lee B. Stern and Co sold three million bushels of November, Cargill Investor Services sold three million November, ADM Investor Services sold two million November and sold three million January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 40,000,down from 51,091 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options Rosenthal Collins bought 1,500 November $8.25 calls at 15 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 November $7.50 puts and sold 1,000 November $7.00 puts at three cents and Prudential Securities bought 500 November $8.50 calls at 8-3/4 to nine cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 23,500, down from 26,307 Thursday.
